You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/selftests/i915_gem_gtt.c`**
   - The error handling in the `fake_dma_object` function has been modified to prevent leaking the gem object.
   - If the allocation of the gem object fails (`if (!obj)`), the code now jumps to the `err` label instead of returning an error pointer directly.
   - If the pinning of the backing storage fails (`if (i915_gem_object_pin_pages(obj))`), the code now jumps to the `err_obj` label, where the gem object is properly released using `i915_gem_object_put(obj)` before returning an error pointer.
   - The return statements have been adjusted to ensure that the function cleans up resources correctly in case of errors.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the `fake_dma_object` function are interrelated in that they both address the same issue of resource management. The changes ensure that if either the allocation of the gem object or the pinning of its backing storage fails, the function will properly clean up by releasing the gem object before returning an error. This prevents memory leaks and ensures that all allocated resources are managed correctly, thereby improving the robustness of the code.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug is caused by the failure to properly release the allocated gem object when either the allocation of the object or the pinning of its backing storage fails. This results in a memory leak, as the gem object remains allocated but is not referenced or used, leading to untracked memory usage.
        
        Commit message:
        drm/i915/selftests: don't leak the gem object

For our fake dma objects we can leak the underlying gem object if we
fail to pin our "backing storage".

v2: use onion teardown and favour i915_gem_object_put

Fixes: 8d28ba4568f4 ("drm/i915: Exercise filling the top/bottom portions of the ppgtt")
Signed-off-by: Matthew Auld <matthew.auld@intel.com>
Cc: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Joonas Lahtinen <joonas.lahtinen@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Joonas Lahtinen <joonas.lahtinen@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20170306235414.23407-2-matthew.auld@intel.com
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>  
        
        Patch:
         
 static struct drm_i915_gem_object *
 fake_dma_object(struct drm_i915_private *i915, u64 size)
 {
 	struct drm_i915_gem_object *obj;
 
 	GEM_BUG_ON(!size);
 	GEM_BUG_ON(!IS_ALIGNED(size, I915_GTT_PAGE_SIZE));
 
 	if (overflows_type(size, obj->base.size))
 		return ERR_PTR(-E2BIG);
 
 	obj = i915_gem_object_alloc(i915);
 	if (!obj)
-		return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM);
+		goto err;
 
 	drm_gem_private_object_init(&i915->drm, &obj->base, size);
 	i915_gem_object_init(obj, &fake_ops);
 
 	obj->base.write_domain = I915_GEM_DOMAIN_CPU;
 	obj->base.read_domains = I915_GEM_DOMAIN_CPU;
 	obj->cache_level = I915_CACHE_NONE;
 
 	/* Preallocate the "backing storage" */
 	if (i915_gem_object_pin_pages(obj))
-		return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM);
+		goto err_obj;
 
 	i915_gem_object_unpin_pages(obj);
 	return obj;
+
+err_obj:
+	i915_gem_object_put(obj);
+err:
+	return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM);
 }
